title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages): Π_0 is the free group on two generators λ0, λ1, with λ0λ1λ∞ = 1. It is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, realised as the free congruence-type subgroup of SL(2,Z) generated by l_0^{-1} = (1 2; 0 1) and l_1 = (1 0; 2 1). M = Π_0^{ab} is a rank-2 lattice with basis λ0, λ1 and λ∞ = −λ0 − λ1. It carries an S_3-type action: ρ_M cyclically permutes λ0 → λ1 → λ∞, σ_M is an involution permuting the λ's, and τ_M = −id. Z_{ρ,σ} and N_{ρ,σ} are group schemes over S_0 (essentially an open of Spec Z). They parametrise (μ, α0, β0) solving the linear 'local' equation (96)/(105) in M_0. The work belongs to the continuation of La Longue Marche, studying how the S_3-symmetry of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} lifts to the 2-step quotients of π1.

Top of page. On the previous page N_{ρ,σ} was shown to be a closed subscheme of Z_{ρ,σ}, smooth (hence flat) over S_0, and equal to Z_{ρ,σ} away from the prime 3. Flatness then gives (107): N_{ρ,σ} is the schematic closure of Z_{ρ,σ} restricted to Spec Z minus {3}. Closure of a subgroup scheme over a Dedekind base is again a subgroup scheme, because closure commutes with fibre products of flat schemes. So N is a subgroup scheme.

Main computation (108). M_0 = Z(λ1−λ0) + Z·3λ1 = Zδ ⊕ Z(1−ρ_M)δ = Zδ + Zρ_Mδ, with δ = λ1−λ0. Check: ρδ = λ∞−λ1 = −λ0−2λ1 = δ − 3λ1, so (1−ρ)δ = 3λ1. In coordinates M_0 = {aλ0+bλ1 : a+b ≡ 0 mod 3}, an index-3 sublattice; det(δ, ρδ) = 3. Equivalently M_0 = (1−ρ)M, the prime ideal above 3 if M is viewed as the Eisenstein lattice Z[ρ]. This explains why 3 is the bad prime in (107).

(109) M_0 contains (1−ρ_M)M and (1−σ_M)M. Hence it is stable under ρ, σ and τ = −id, so it is normalised by the whole symmetry group 𝔊. Its preimage in Π_0 is therefore a normal subgroup, containing [Π_0, Π_0], of index 3, and normal in the ambient group (𝔊_0, roughly the group of GL(2,Z)-type symmetries).

Next page. Grothendieck conjectures that this subgroup is a congruence subgroup of level 12 and index 36 in SL(2,Z), with image of order 32 in SL(2,Z/12). Verification: Π_0 = ⟨(1 2;0 1), (1 0;2 1)⟩ = {γ ∈ Γ(2) : a ≡ d ≡ 1 mod 4} has level 4 and index 12. The character a+b mod 3 equals the abelianisation character SL(2,F_3) → Z/3 restricted to Π_0, because l0 ≡ (1 1;0 1) and l1 ≡ (1 0;−1 1), which are conjugate in SL(2,F_3). Hence the subgroup equals Π_0 ∩ preimage of Q_8. It contains Γ(12) and has index 36. Its image in SL(2,Z/4) × SL(2,Z/3) has order 4·8 = 32. The guess is correct.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The basis claim Zδ ⊕ Z(1−ρ_M)δ is correct, with determinant 3 relative to (λ0, λ1).

The congruence guess formulated on the next page (level 12, index 36, order 32 in SL(2,Z/12)) is in fact true. This follows from the identification of the index-3 character with the SL(2,F_3)^{ab} character.

ideas.what: N_{ρ,σ} is flat (smooth) over the base, so it is the schematic closure of its restriction away from p=3, hence a subgroup scheme
ideas.modern_name: schematic closure of a flat subgroup scheme over a Dedekind base

ideas.what: The index-3 sublattice M_0 = (1−ρ)M of Π_0^{ab}, stable under the S_3 × {±1} symmetries, giving a characteristic-type index-3 normal subgroup of the free group π1(P^1 − {0,1,∞})
ideas.modern_name: Eisenstein ideal (1−ζ_3) in Z[ζ_3]; index-3 abelian cover of P^1 minus 3 points (the Fermat-cubic-type cover)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (circulated) discusses Π_0^{ab} and its symmetries; this specific computation is unsure

ideas.what: Recognising the corresponding subgroup of SL(2,Z) as a congruence subgroup of level 12 (Π_0 ∩ Γ(3)·Q_8-preimage)
ideas.modern_name: congruence subgroups of level 12 / Fermat curve of degree 3 as modular curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein–Fricke; Rohrlich for Fermat curves as modular curves)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping inside a longer computation of group schemes attached to the symmetries of Π_0^{ab}. The index-3 sublattice and its congruence-subgroup interpretation are classical (the Fermat cubic is a modular curve). The flatness/closure argument is standard.
